title: Choose a motion method
target: Choose a motion relationship and justify its assumptions.
criteria: Choose a relationship using the known quantities.
Show linked calculations with units and directions.
State when constant velocity or acceleration applies.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Given initial velocity, constant acceleration, and elapsed time, which relation directly gives final velocity?
cpa.guide: Use the relation connecting the specified quantities.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Given initial and final velocities and constant acceleration, but no time, which relation can find displacement?
cpa.guide: This equation eliminates time for constant acceleration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A rover starts at +3 m/s and accelerates at +2 m/s² for 4 s. What is final velocity?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A cart starts from rest and reaches 8 m/s in 4 s with constant acceleration. What are average velocity and displacement?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: When is Δx = vt with one fixed v justified over an interval?
options: Only when the object starts at the origin.
When velocity is constant throughout the interval.
Whenever the final speed is known.
cpa.guide: A fixed velocity must describe the entire interval, or v must explicitly be the average.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A motor’s force varies substantially during a run. Can one constant-acceleration formula automatically describe the whole run?
options: Yes; changing force never affects acceleration.
Yes; every motor produces constant acceleration.
No; motion cannot be analyzed at all.
No; justify an approximation or model the varying acceleration.
cpa.guide: Fixed mass with varying net force generally has varying acceleration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
